reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) from a single paper directly supports the premises: it states that coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, demonstrates SCCP in a tungsten-based HEA, and reports high strength and ductility at 800 °C. However, the evidence is from one study and the hypothesis extends the mechanism to toughness and delayed failure, which are not explicitly measured in the cited work.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission
Coherent nanoprecipitates relieve stress concentrations that cause crack initiation
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation (SCCP) can be achieved in tungsten-based refractory HEAs
SCCP-treated alloys show improved ductility and toughness at high temperatures (≥800 °C)
The mechanism operates in a BCC matrix under high-temperature tensile conditions
